summary: Andrew Goudie is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Dean Close School (~1958–1963) and Trinity Hall (1964–1970). He served as a professor and head at the University of Oxford from 1970 to 2014.

Indologist Andrew Henry Yarrow earned degrees from UNC Chapel Hill and Yale University, studying under Franklin Edgerton. He taught Sanskrit at Yale, was an assistant professor at Columbia University (1952), and served as a professor at the University of Miami.

Andrew Hollingworth Frost was an Indology and linguistics scholar who earned his B.A. at St John's College (1838–1842). He served as principal of Church Missionary Society College, Islington (1870–1874) and lectured at the University of Cambridge (1884–1902).

Specializing in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies, Andrew J. Nicholson studied under Sri Narayana Mishra. As attested in 2026, he serves as an associate professor and Director of the Program in South Asian Studies at Stony Brook University.
Andrew Jukes was an Indology and linguistics scholar who was educated at Blundell's School. From 1878 to 1906, he served as a medical missionary for the Church Mission Society.

Andrew Olendzki is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Lancaster University and under Masatoshi Nagatomi. He served as executive director at the Insight Meditation Society, and held leadership and scholar positions at the Barre Center and Mind and Life Institute.

Indology and linguistics scholar Andrew Ollett studied at the University of Oxford (~2008–2010) and Columbia University (~2010–2016). Around 2023, he served as an associate professor at the University of Chicago.

Andrew P. Tuck works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Princeton University and was taught by Victor Preller, Jeffrey Stout, William E. Kennick, Robert A. F. Thurman, and John Pemberton.
Andrew Quintman is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Jay L. Garfield. He served as an assistant professor in the Department of Religious Studies at Yale University.

Andrew Sihler is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard and Yale, earning his doctorate under Warren Crawford Cowgill (~1963–1967). He held a post at the University of Wisconsin-Madison from approximately 1967 to 1998.

Andrew Stirling was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at East India Company College (1811–1812) and Fort William College (~1813–1814), he served in the East India Company's Political Department (~1828–1830).

Specializing in Japanology and history/archaeology, Andrew Watsky studied at Oberlin College (~1975–1979) and Princeton University (~1988–1994). He served on the faculty at Vassar College from approximately 1994 to 2008.
Andrew William Kennedy is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leeds (attested 2006) under the supervision of Philip A. Mellor and Kim Knott.

Indologist and linguist Andrey Klebanov earned his degrees at the University of Hamburg, studying with Harunaga Isaacson and others. He has held academic posts at Kyoto University, the University of Alberta, the University of Vienna, and the University of Hamburg.

Andrey Terentyev is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and the Russian Academy of Sciences. He held a post at the Museum of History of Religion from approximately 1978 to 1988.
Andrey Zaliznyak studied under André Martinet from approximately 1956 to 1957 and under Vyacheslav Ivanov from approximately 1956 to 1960.

Andrzej Gawroński was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Lviv and Leipzig under Ernst Windisch and others. He held academic posts at Jagiellonian University, the University of Warsaw, and as Professor of Indology at the University of Lviv.

Andrzej Ługowski was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Adam Mickiewicz University and the University of Warsaw, supervised by Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz. He taught at the University of Warsaw from approximately 1968 to 2004.

András Róna-Tas is a linguist and scholar of Tibetology and Iranian/Central Asian studies. Educated at Eötvös Loránd University and the Hungarian Academy of Sciences, he was a longtime professor at the University of Szeged (1968–2002) and president of IATS.

André Bareau was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar educated at ENS, the Sorbonne, EPHE, and Collège de France. He held research positions at the CNRS, served as Directeur d'Études at EPHE, and was a professor at Collège de France.
